description: Node.js CLI tool that analyzes Markdown files for word count, reading time, and heading structure

userStories.title: Project scaffolding with TypeScript, Commander, and Vitest
userStories.description:
Set up the md-analyzer Node.js project from scratch.

Create the following structure:
```
md-analyzer/
  src/
    cli.ts          # Commander setup, entry point
    analyzer.ts     # Core analysis logic (pure functions, empty stubs)
    formatter.ts    # Output formatting (empty stubs)
  tests/
    fixtures/
      sample.md     # Test fixture with known word count and headings
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  vitest.config.ts
  README.md
```

package.json requirements:
- name: md-analyzer
- type: module (ESM)
- bin: { "md-analyzer": "./dist/cli.js" }
- scripts: build (tsc), test (vitest), start (node dist/cli.js)
- dependencies: commander
- devDependencies: typescript, vitest, @types/node

tsconfig.json: strict mode, target ES2022, module NodeNext, moduleResolution NodeNext, outDir dist, rootDir src.

vitest.config.ts: basic config.

cli.ts should set up Commander with:
- Program name 'md-analyzer', description, version from package.json
- Command: analyze <file> with --json and --wpm <number> options
- For now, the analyze command can print 'Not yet implemented'

The project must build with `npm run build` and `npx md-analyzer --help` must show usage.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json has type: module, correct bin entry, and all required deps
tsconfig.json compiles with strict mode and ESM output
npm run build succeeds with zero errors
npx md-analyzer --help prints usage information
npx md-analyzer --version prints version number
Directory structure matches the spec
vitest.config.ts exists and npm test runs (even if no tests yet)
tests/fixtures/sample.md exists with sample Markdown content

userStories.title: Implement Markdown analyzer core functions
userStories.description:
Implement the core analysis logic in src/analyzer.ts.

Functions to implement:

1. `countWords(content: string): number`
   - Count words in Markdown content
   - Exclude fenced code blocks (``` ... ```)
   - Strip inline HTML tags before counting
   - Split on whitespace, filter empty strings

2. `calculateReadingTime(wordCount: number, wpm?: number): { minutes: number; seconds: number; text: string }`
   - Default wpm = 200
   - minutes and seconds are the broken-down reading time
   - text is human-readable like '2 min read' or '< 1 min read'

3. `extractHeadings(content: string): Heading[]`
   - Parse ATX headings: /^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/gm
   - Return tree structure: { level: number; text: string; children: Heading[] }
   - Top-level array contains h1s (or lowest level found), nested appropriately
   - Headings inside fenced code blocks should be excluded

4. `analyzeFile(filePath: string): Promise<AnalysisResult>`
   - Read file from disk using node:fs/promises
   - Run countWords, calculateReadingTime, extractHeadings
   - Return combined AnalysisResult
   - Throw descriptive error if file doesn't exist

Type exports:
```typescript
export interface Heading {
  level: number;
  text: string;
  children: Heading[];
}

export interface AnalysisResult {
  filePath: string;
  wordCount: number;
  readingTime: { minutes: number; seconds: number; text: string };
  headings: Heading[];
}
```

Write unit tests in tests/analyzer.test.ts covering:
- countWords: plain text, with code blocks, with HTML tags, empty string
- calculateReadingTime: various word counts, custom WPM, zero words
- extractHeadings: flat headings, nested headings, no headings, code block headings excluded
- analyzeFile: valid file (use fixture), missing file throws

Use vitest. All imports use .js extensions. Use node: prefix for builtins.
acceptanceCriteria: countWords correctly counts words excluding code blocks and HTML
calculateReadingTime returns correct minutes/seconds/text
extractHeadings returns correct tree structure for nested headings
extractHeadings excludes headings inside fenced code blocks
analyzeFile reads a file and returns combined AnalysisResult
analyzeFile throws on missing file with descriptive error
All analyzer tests pass
npm run build succeeds

userStories.title: Implement output formatter (text and JSON)
userStories.description:
Implement output formatting in src/formatter.ts.

Functions:

1. `formatText(result: AnalysisResult): string`
   Pretty-print results for terminal output. Format:
   ```
   File: README.md
   Words: 1,234
   Reading time: 6 min read

   Headings:
     # Introduction
       ## Getting Started
       ## Installation
     # Usage
       ## CLI Options
   ```
   - Word count should use locale formatting (commas for thousands)
   - Headings indented by 2 spaces per level (h1 = 2 spaces, h2 = 4 spaces, etc.)
   - If no headings, print 'Headings: (none)'

2. `formatJson(result: AnalysisResult): string`
   - JSON.stringify with 2-space indentation
   - Must produce valid, parseable JSON

Write tests in tests/formatter.test.ts:
- formatText produces expected output format with known input
- formatText handles zero words, no headings
- formatText formats word count with commas
- formatJson produces valid JSON
- formatJson round-trips (parse output matches input)

Import AnalysisResult type from ./analyzer.js (ESM .js extension).
acceptanceCriteria: formatText produces correctly formatted terminal output
Word count uses comma formatting for thousands
Heading tree is properly indented in text output
formatJson produces valid parseable JSON
All formatter tests pass
npm run build succeeds

userStories.title: Wire CLI analyze command with full pipeline
userStories.description:
Connect the CLI entry point (src/cli.ts) to the analyzer and formatter.

The analyze command should:
1. Accept a positional <file> argument (required)
2. Options: --json (boolean, default false), --wpm <number> (default 200)
3. Call analyzeFile(file) from analyzer.ts
4. If --json, call formatJson and print to stdout
5. If not --json, call formatText and print to stdout
6. On error (file not found, read error): print error to stderr, exit with code 1
7. On success: exit with code 0

Make `analyze` the default command so both work:
- `md-analyzer analyze README.md`
- `md-analyzer README.md` (shorthand)

Write integration tests in tests/cli.test.ts:
- Run the built CLI against tests/fixtures/sample.md
- Verify stdout contains word count, reading time, headings
- Verify --json flag produces valid JSON
- Verify --wpm flag changes reading time
- Verify missing file prints error to stderr and exits with code 1
- Verify --help and --version work

Use child_process.execFile in tests to run the actual CLI binary.
Tests should run `npm run build` in a beforeAll or assume dist/ is built.
acceptanceCriteria: md-analyzer analyze <file> outputs word count, reading time, and headings
md-analyzer <file> works as shorthand (default command)
--json flag outputs valid JSON to stdout
--wpm flag changes reading time calculation
Missing file prints error to stderr and exits with code 1
--help and --version flags work
All CLI integration tests pass
npm run build succeeds

userStories.title: End-to-end tests and coverage verification
userStories.description:
Add end-to-end smoke tests and verify test coverage.

1. Create a comprehensive test fixture at tests/fixtures/complex.md:
   - Multiple heading levels (h1 through h4)
   - Fenced code blocks with headings inside (should be excluded)
   - Inline HTML tags
   - At least 500 words for meaningful reading time
   - Known expected values documented in a comment at top of test file

2. Add e2e test in tests/e2e.test.ts:
   - Analyze complex.md fixture, verify exact word count
   - Verify reading time calculation matches expected
   - Verify heading tree structure matches expected
   - Verify JSON output round-trips correctly
   - Verify text output matches expected snapshot

3. Verify coverage:
   - Run vitest with coverage
   - Ensure 90%+ line coverage across analyzer.ts, formatter.ts, cli.ts
   - Add coverage config to vitest.config.ts if not present

4. Final cleanup:
   - Ensure README.md documents usage
   - Ensure package.json 'files' field includes dist/
   - Run npm pack --dry-run to verify publishable
acceptanceCriteria: Complex test fixture exists with known expected values
E2E tests verify exact word count, reading time, and heading structure
JSON output round-trip test passes
All tests pass (unit + integration + e2e)
Test coverage is 90%+ across all source files
npm pack --dry-run succeeds
README.md documents usage with examples
